Hi Tom

Thanks again for the call earlier - great to learn more about Finch's telemetry and privacy needs. Per our discussion, here's a short recap and the next steps I promised: 

1) Current asks from your security/privacy team:
   - PII classification and automatic redaction for stored logs (PII types: name, email, SSN-like identifiers)
   - Data retention policy: 30 days for request logs, 365 days for billing metadata, ability to configure retention windows
   - Detailed logging controls: token-level usage logs, request/response hashes (redacted), and audit trails for access
   - Data residency: primary storage in us-west-2 with optional eu-west-1 for EU customers
   - Encryption: in-transit TLS 1.2+ and at-rest AES-256; preference for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)

2) What Redwood provides today (summary):
   - TLS 1.3 for all API traffic, mTLS option for Dedicated/Private deployments
   - At-rest encryption with AES-256; support for customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) on Dedicated and Private
   - Audit logs (object-level) delivered to your S3/Cloud Storage or our secure log sink; configurable retention and export
   - Data residency controls for Private deployments and Dedicated zones; Hosted accounts are region-configurable at provisioning

3) Action items / next steps:
   - I attached a short KMS options doc and an architecture diagram that outlines CMK flows and key rotation (redwood-kms-options.pdf, kms-arch-diagram.png).
   - Sean (cc'd) can join a 30–45 min security deep-dive next week to walk your infosec team through HSM/KMS flows and provide a short threat model.
   - Tom / Natalie: please share an initial list of compliance artifacts you need (SOC 2 sections, encryption attestations) - I attached a SOC2 summary as a starter.

If that looks right, I'll set up the security session for next Tue/Wed.

Best,

Hi Tom - great questions; answering inline below and attaching the KMS architecture PDF for details.

> For PII redaction: can Redwood provide both on-the-fly redaction (before write) and post-ingest redaction workflows?
Yes - we support both approaches: 
  - Pre-ingest (client-side or gateway redaction): recommended for highest privacy guarantees; we provide SDK hooks and a configurable field-mapping that can run in your VPC or client-side before hitting Redwood.
  - Post-ingest: configurable Redaction Jobs in Redwood Console that can scan and redact stored logs based on regex/patterns and ML classifiers. We can set up redaction retention and audit logs for those jobs.

> Key management: Finch would prefer CMK with HSM backing where Redwood acts as a key consumer (i.e., customer-managed, not Redwood-managed). For Hosted, is there a model where CMKs are in our AWS account but Redwood can still perform seamless key access for inference?
Short answer: yes - we support a cross-account CMK model for Hosted via an AWS KMS grant model. The flow: CMKs are created in the customer AWS account (or GCP CMEK) and Redwood requests short-lived grants scoped to encryption/decryption operations for inference. For environments requiring FIPS/HSM attestations, we support Dedicated and Private deployments where HSM-backed keys remain under your control and Redwood services run in a dedicated tenant network with KMS access controlled via IAM/GRANT. See attached diagram for flow and key rotation recommendations.

> Logging: we need an immutable audit trail for key use (decrypt/sign) events for at least 365 days.
We can emit key-use events to your cloud audit log (CloudTrail/Syslog) and also mirror logs to your S3/GCS bucket with object immutability options. For Hosted, we retain key-use metadata for 365 days by default for enterprise customers; for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and immutability policies.

> Tokenized request/response material stored by Redwood for up to 30 days for debugging, and whether that can be disabled per-tenant?
By default, short-lived request traces are kept for 7-30 days depending on plan; we offer a per-tenant setting to disable request body retention (you can retain only hashed metadata). We'll include an opt-out flag for Finch on provisioning so no request bodies are stored.

- I'll upload a more detailed KMS playbook to the Drive link and share a HubSpot note with the proposed configuration.

Thanks - see attached files.
